text:
sam: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression in prod after the runtime deploy this morning. tail latency for multi-GPU tensor-parallel requests jumped ~2x. nsight traces point to all-reduce stalls coinciding with graph replay events.

tia: Which deploy hash? any rollout percentage data?

sam: rollout 12% (canary). commit 3f4a2b9 changed kernel-selection stream assignment + batching heuristic. infra-bot reported increased P50->P95.

alex: Noted. I pushed a kernel-selection tweak last week to prefer fused kernels on longer sequences. That also changed which CUDA stream we bind for capture. Could be stream ordering regression.

maria: We rely on CUDA graphs + prefix KV caching. If capture/replay happens on a different stream priority or with different event sync, all-reduce ops (NCCL) can end up waiting. Seen similar subtle stalls before.

sam: Pasted a trimmed nsys timeline snapshot (timestamps are relative):

```
0.000s: enqueue kernel A on stream s1 (compute)
0.002s: capture graph on stream s2 (capture)
0.0025s: replay graph on s2
0.003s: ncclAllReduce launched on stream s1
0.0031s: s1 tries to access kv cache memory, but replay on s2 has outstanding memcpy
0.0032s: event sync from s2 -> s1 (host sync) -> s1 stalled 0.9ms
0.0042s: allreduce runs after host sync
```

nsys-bot: collected trace: /artifacts/nsys/1765550000_trace.qdrep (10MB)

tia: That host-sync step is the killer. Do we have any cross-stream event inserts in the capture path now?

alex: The kernel selector change added an async prefetch that uses a temporary stream for kv prefetch and relies on captured graphs for replay. I may have left an implicit cudaDeviceSynchronize when switching capture contexts.

maria: Also saw more frequent graph replays when batching heuristics fold short sequences into a captured path. More replays -> more opportunities for ordering gaps.

sam: Repro on devpool/gpu-4 by running the exact workload with seq distribution (long tail). I can reproduce 95th latency spike when I enable graph replay + async prefetch.

alex: Action idea: keep kernel selection change but force capture stream to be the same as compute stream (avoid cross-stream replays), or ensure we use cudaStreamWaitEvent instead of host-side sync. Which is safer short-term?

maria: cudaStreamWaitEvent is better — avoids host roundtrip. But we must ensure events are recorded on the correct stream during capture so replay semantics are preserved.

tia: Quick mitigation: rollback the kernel-selection change in canary (3f4a2b9 -> 2e9c1a4) and reduce canary to 0%. That buys time for a proper fix.

infra-bot: deploy rollback triggered: canary set to 0% by @tia at 08:44. Monitoring. :eyes: 

sam: For the fix I propose: 1) change prefetch to record event on capture stream; 2) use streamWaitEvent on compute stream before allreduce; 3) add unit test that simulates capture+replay across streams.

alex: I'll prepare a patch. quick prototype diff: 
```
- cudaMemcpyAsync(..., prefetch_stream);
- cudaEventRecord(evt, prefetch_stream);
- cudaDeviceSynchronize(); // implicit host sync
+ cudaMemcpyAsync(..., capture_stream);
+ cudaEventRecord(evt, capture_stream);
+ cudaStreamWaitEvent(compute_stream, evt, 0);
```

maria: Make sure to set event flags to cudaEventDisableTiming | cudaEventInterprocessHandle if needed. Also check priority of capture_stream vs compute_stream (we used low-priority for background operations previously).

tia: Tests to run before re-rollout: reproduce on devpool (4 GPUs), run nsight capture with capture_mode=stream, run stress with mixed seq lengths, verify no host-sync spikes, and add prometheus histograms for event-wait durations.

sam: I'll attach the dev repro script and the trace. repro gist: https://internal/gists/graph-repro-1765550000 (contains run profile and env).

alex: I'll open PR with tests + fix and mark WIP. If we can't get a clean fix in 2h, we'll keep rollback in place and schedule an on-call deep dive.

maria: Also add a guard: if graph replay count > threshold in a single request path, fall back to non-captured path (avoid chaining replays). Could be a safety valve.

sam: Agreed. thanks all — next steps: alex PR, sam/ti validate repro, maria add safety gate, tia confirm rollback metrics trending back to baseline.

infra-bot: monitoring: P95 tail latency returning toward baseline after rollback. will post updated dashboard in 10m. :white_check_mark:
